findings.element: .b-stepRead — the editor's date readout, owner-editing and owner-undone
findings.problem: The readout is built as longYear + "\u00a0\u00b7 in " + dayCount (render-b.js:712 and :1014). The nbsp binds the middot backwards so it can never open line 2 — which is what interaction-check.mjs's 'the connector cannot start a line' asserts. But the string does not fit its measure, so the break simply moves to the other side of the same glyph and the separator is left hanging at the end of line 1. Measured on BOTH grounds with per-line client rects: at 390 the measure is 332px and the lines set 230px / 96px; at 1152, 1280 and 1440 the rail measure is 310px and the lines set 230px / 96px. Identical on paper and on ink. So the visible result is 'Saturday 8 August 2026 ·' with the dot standing 80–100px clear of anything, then 'in 23 days' below it — a lone separator floating in white space, which at 15px Geist Mono with 0.04em reads as a truncation mark or a typo rather than a connector. This is the only piece of typographic litter I found in 308 renders. It is not the settled 'stepread-never-fits-its-measure' (round 8): that finding claimed the readout NEVER sets on one line and that the two-line reserve was wrong; I accept both refutations — the reserve is right and the 701–1023 band does set on one line. My claim is narrower and its evidence is the refutation's own: at the widths where it DOES wrap, the connector ends a line. The gate solved half this problem and the other half is still on screen. Round 10 fixed the connector's head; nothing looked at its tail.
findings.fix: BUILD — it changes a currently-passing assertion, so it goes on the founder's list rather than being made mid-round. Stop making the two facts one sentence and set them as the two lines the 45px reserve already pays for. In render-b.js:1014 replace the single text node with two children of .b-stepRead — h("span", { text: F.fmt.longYear(iso) }) and h("span", { text: "in " + F.fmt.dayCount(away) }) — and mirror the same two-node rewrite in the live update at render-b.js:712 so the status region still repaints in place. In b.css:808 add `.b-stepRead > span { display: block }` and drop `text-wrap: balance` from that rule (it has nothing left to balance); keep min-height: 45px, the mono family, --size-body, --lead-label and --track-data untouched, so the reserve, the ladder and the tabular figures are unchanged and the 701–1023 band gains a second line inside room already reserved for it — no reflow at any width, on either ground. Then retire interaction-check.mjs's 'the connector cannot start a line' block (around L2688): it exists only to police a connector that no longer exists, and it will fail on indexOf("\u00b7") === -1. Replace it with an assertion that earns its keep — that .b-stepRead sets on exactly two lines and that neither line's last non-space character is \u00b7, \u2013 or \u2014 — run on both grounds, which is the property that was actually wanted. The role="status" announcement improves too: 'Saturday 8 August 2026, in 23 days' instead of a spoken middot.

biggestWin: The ramp is a contract, not a habit, and it holds identically in both rooms. Driving all fourteen states at 320/390/701/768/1023/1024/1152/1279/1280/1440/1920 on paper and on ink — 308 renders — the whole surface resolves to 28 distinct type settings. Every one sits on the declared 13-step size ladder; every size carries exactly one tracking value, never two; every leading is one of the six declared steps. Two weights do real hierarchy work rather than decorating it: the lead moment sets at 600 and everything behind it at 400 at the same 17/24px size, so three row states are told apart by weight and ink density with no third weight and no second hue. The display tier is graded rather than scaled — 148, 96 and 64 each carry their own letterfit, and the word that replaces the count on the morning gets a separate step because it is letters and not figures. Underneath that, the discipline that usually goes missing: text-wrap balance or pretty on every prose block, non-breaking spaces binding every date, and across all 308 renders not one orphan, not one widow, not one line of horizontal page scroll, and — excluding the sr-only nodes — not one clipped or overflowing text box, at 320px as well as 1920. I stress-typed a 68-character moment title into the editor at nine widths on both grounds: the trim is word-safe every time, sets a real U+2026, and keeps the full string in the title attribute; zero mid-word cuts. The marks are a typographer's, not a keyboard's — U+2212 in the step buttons, U+2014 in the cancelled row, U+00B7 as the connector, tabular figures wired globally through .num. And the two rooms render byte-identical type metrics, so nothing in this system is keyed to one ink ladder. This is the level of care Vercel's own Geist specimen shows, and it is ready for Home, Notes and Tasks to inherit — with one caveat worth an hour: shell.css binds --lead-head to '24, 30, 38px' while both 38px titles ship at --lead-title (1.06). The render is right and the comment is stale, but that comment is about to become three more products' type contract, so fix the comment, not the setting.
